paragraphs.text: Wellington IC R1068 of 21 Operational Training Unit took off from Moreton-in-Marsh on a cross-country training flight on 17 August 1941 and crashed on Ffridd Rhosfarch, above Pennal. Chorley's Bomber Command Losses places the crash about three miles west of Machynlleth and puts the aircraft with A Flight. All six men on board were killed.

Sources give different times. Chorley says the aircraft emerged from cloud and crashed at 1150. History Points says it took off at 11am with a pupil crew and a more experienced navigator, and crashed at about 11.40am.

History Points says no definite cause could be established, and that the crew were thought to have glimpsed the Dyfi estuary through cloud and taken it for the sea. Coflein records navigational error on breaking through the cloud.

The crew were Sgt James Francis Paul Stuart RCAF (pilot, 21, from Cornwall, Ontario), P/O George Joyce Matthews (observer, of Olverston, Bristol), Sgt Herbert George Mole (27, of Kew, Surrey), Sgt H George Hewison (air gunner, 30, of Benwell, Newcastle), Sgt John Francis Moore (wireless operator/air gunner, 21, of Janesboro, Limerick) and Sgt Allan Jackets (wireless operator/air gunner, 21, of Hull).

Stuart and Moore are buried in Tywyn Cemetery. Chorley says the other four were claimed by their next of kin: Hewison lies in Newcastle, Jackets in Hull, Matthews at Cottesmore in Rutland and Mole in Plaistow, east London.

The memorial is a plaque beside the village war memorial at Pennal, in Gwynedd, not a marker at the crash site. IBCC transcribes its text as: To the memory of six members of the RAF who died for freedom when their plane crashed on "Ffridd Rhosfarch" 17th August 1941.

Sources describe the plaque differently. War Memorials Online records a brass plaque with an RAF badge, dedication and names, on the cemetery wall with a grey granite surround. Coflein records a slate slab in an alcove in the stone wall behind the village war memorial. IBCC calls it an inscribed metal plaque. Chorley says the plaque is in the local church, which none of the other sources support.
We found no source that says who erected the plaque, when it was dedicated, or who looks after it.

retractions.reason: Wrexham Royal British Legion: no source links any RBL branch to this memorial; Pennal is in Gwynedd.
'Wrexham Royal British Legion supports the memorial' has no source.
Generated text names a Robert Thomas as a casualty; no source places him on R1068 (six other men are named by Chorley, IBCC and History Points). Replaced by the sourced narrative.
'Crash site marker' is wrong: the memorial is a plaque beside the village war memorial at Pennal (IBCC, WMO, Coflein).

notes:
MEMORIAL IS NOT A CRASH-SITE MARKER. Our record has memorial_type 'Crash site marker' and coordinates/what3words for Ffridd Rhosfarch. Every source that describes the memorial places it at Pennal village, beside the village war memorial by the A493 and cemetery wall: IBCC (all six loss pages, 'Adjacent to village war memorial, Pennal'), War Memorials Online (WMO/227082, brass plaque on cemetery wall), Coflein 420058 (slate slab in alcove behind the village memorial), History Points. The crash site is separate: Coflein 515293 gives OS grid SH6880002500 (Protected Place, small wreckage fragments). Our lat/long 52.6048,-3.9411 and what3words tweed.allows.drop are unsourced; I could not check them against the grid reference here (no coordinate converter), so a human should convert SH6880002500 and decide whether the record should carry the memorial point (Pennal, near SH 7008 0041 where Coflein places the village memorial) or the crash site. Coordinates and what3words are not retractable via dossier. IWM's entry for the village cross (WMR 13365) lists 16 WW1 and 3 WW2 names and says nothing about the airmen's plaque; I found no IWM record for the plaque, so I made no IWM claim. A separate IWM entry may be worth a submission.
CONFLICT, PLAQUE LOCATION AND MATERIAL: Chorley (1990s book, via reader) says the plaque is in the local church. IBCC, WMO, Coflein and History Points place it at the village war memorial / cemetery wall. WMO says brass, Coflein says slate, IBCC says metal plaque. Both versions are in the memorial_details paragraph; a photo or site visit would settle it. The dossier gives memorial_type Board / Plaque / Tablet (WMO) only. WMO's own text says the plaque carries names; IBCC's inscription may be only the dedication line, so the inscription field may be partial. WMO has no photos and no condition level.
TIMES: Chorley 1150 crash; History Points took off 11am, crashed about 11.40am. Both in the narrative, unreconciled.
CAUSE: 'Mistook the Dyfi estuary for the sea' is NOT unsourced after all: History Points ('it was thought') and Coflein (stated as the cause) both carry it. Kept, attributed as suspected. Coflein and History Points may share an origin (neither names its source for it beyond a list of books on Coflein), so treat as lightly corroborated.
ROBERT THOMAS: no source places a Robert Thomas on this aircraft. Chorley lists six other names; IBCC, History Points and Coflein agree on six. The only 'Robert Thomas' hits were unrelated menu text on historypoints.org (a Caernarfon house). Retracted with the narrative. Not searched further for a different crash.
RBL CONTACT: no source links Wrexham Royal British Legion to this memorial (Pennal is in Gwynedd, nowhere near Wrexham). Retracted local_contacts and community_connection.
CUSTODIAN: unknown. Leads: Pennal Community Council, St Peter ad Vincula church, Rab Jones and Phillip Jones (credited by History Points; not named in any custodian role), Machynlleth RBL. status 'unknown' not 'unknown-confirmed' because I did not ask any of them.
NAMES AND ROLES: Hewison: IBCC 'H George Hewison' (Chorley H G); History Points 'George Hewison'. I used the IBCC form and made no History Points name claim for him; his CWGC forename is unchecked. Mole role: IBCC 2nd Pilot, History Points Pilot (conflict claim kept, resolves to IBCC by tier; left out of the paragraph). Matthews has no age on IBCC or History Points. Moore is Irish (IBCC country of origin 'Eire'), from Janesboro, Limerick (Chorley, IBCC, History Points). Stuart RCAF, from Cornwall, Ontario. Chorley's ISBN in the reader's email (1.85780.142.6) differs from the cover photo (1-85780-132-6); I left the ISBN out of the citation.
NOT CHECKED: CWGC individual pages (searches returned bulk export listings that agree with IBCC for Stuart, Mole and Jackets on age, number and burial, but I did not read the casualty pages, so no CWGC claims or URLs). ASN (Cloudflare 403). ww1.wales has a page 'Pennal Vickers Wellington R1068 Memorial' in its menu but the URL returned 404, so not read; it may give crew biographies and a fuller description. IBCC was rate-limited once; requests were slowed.
DATA: reader correspondence is not cited by name. Chorley's 'Merioneth' is the historic county; the record's county is now Gwynedd (Coflein).
